Since the focus is on C-O bond formation via catalytic coupling, it qualifies as a coupling reaction. The catalyst is a soluble Cu(I)/1,10-phenanthroline complex operating in solution, making it homogeneous.

title: Unveiling the Synthesis of Indole-Fused Eight-Membered Aza-Heterocycles via FeCl3-Catalyzed Radical C-N Coupling and Photophysical Studies
rationale: FeCl3-catalyzed cross-dehydrogenative double C-N bond formation via radical pathway. The catalyst is a soluble iron salt (FeCl3) used in solution, making it homogeneous. No solid support is involved, and no specific ligand is mentioned. The reaction forms C-N bonds.

title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Regioselective C8-H Sulfoxamination of 1-Naphthylamine Derivatives with NH-Sulfoximines
rationale: The article describes a cobalt-catalyzed cross-dehydrogenative C-H/N-H coupling reaction between 1-naphthylamine derivatives and NH-sulfoximines to form C-N bonds. The catalyst is CoBr2, a soluble metal salt used in a homogeneous system (no solid support mentioned). No specific ligand is named; the picolinamide directing group is part of the substrate, not a catalyst ligand. This is a C-N bond-forming coupling reaction.

title: Nickel-Catalyzed Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling of NHPI Esters to Access 1,4-Dialkylbenzenes
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed decarboxylative cross-coupling reaction forming C(sp2)-C(sp3) bonds between NHPI esters and 1,4-diiodobenzene analogues. The catalyst is a soluble NiBr2·diglyme complex with ligand L1, operating under photochemical conditions, which is homogeneous catalysis.

title: Three-Component Regioselective Aryl- and Alkenyl-Aminoalkylation of Alkenes via Cooperative Photoredox/Nickel Catalysis
rationale: The article describes a three-component aminoalkyl-vinylation of alkenes via synergistic photoredox/nickel catalysis, forming C-C bonds. The catalyst system uses NiBr2·DME (a soluble nickel salt) with bipyridine ligands (4,4-di(OMe)bpy) and an organic photosensitizer (4-CzIPN) in solution, which is homogeneous catalysis.

title: Mechanism and Origin of Nickel-Catalyzed Decarbonylative Construction of C(sp2)-C(sp3) Bonds from Carboxylic Acids and Their Derivatives
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed decarbonylative cross-coupling reaction forming C(sp2)-C(sp3) bonds (C-C bond formation) from carboxylic acids and their derivatives. The catalyst is a molecular nickel complex (Ni(cod)2 mentioned in examples) operating in solution, making it homogeneous. While ligands are mentioned as controlling chemoselectivity, no specific ligand name is provided in the given text.

title: Expedited Aminoglutarimide C-N Cross-Coupling Enabled by High-Throughput Experimentation
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed Buchwald-Hartwig cross-coupling of (hetero)aryl halides with aminoglutarimide to form C-N bonds. The catalyst is a soluble Pd complex (Pd-catalyzed with ligand screening via HTE), indicating homogeneous catalysis. No solid support is mentioned, and the ligand is not specified in the provided text.

title: Cross-Coupling of Carbonyl Derivatives and N-Arylamines Enabled by Visible Light for Easy Access to 1,2-Amino Alcohols
rationale: The article describes a visible-light-driven cross-coupling of carbonyl derivatives and N-arylamines to form 1,2-amino alcohols (C-C bond formation) via an electron-donor-acceptor (EDA) complex. It explicitly states the reaction proceeds 'without the requirement of a photocatalyst and metal,' indicating a homogeneous, metal-free process.

title: Direct Cross-Couplings of Aryl Nonaflates with Aryl Bromides under Nickel Catalysis
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed direct cross-coupling of aryl nonaflates with aryl bromides to form biaryls (C-C bonds). The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (Ni(PPh3)2Cl2, NiCl2, etc.) operating in THF solution, making it homogeneous. The key ligand identified in optimization is PPh3. No solid support is involved.

title: Regioselective Suzuki-Miyarua Cross-Coupling for Substituted 2,4-Dibromopyridines Catalyzed by C3-Symmetric Tripalladium Clusters
rationale: The article describes C3-symmetric tripalladium clusters (soluble molecular complexes) catalyzing Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling (C-C bond formation) of 2,4-dibromopyridines with arylboronic acids/pinacol esters, with extension to Sonogashira, Negishi, and Kumada couplings. The catalyst is a homogeneous molecular cluster, not a solid heterogeneous material.

title: Synthesis of Functionalized Thioimidates from Thioamides and Arylboronic Acids via Copper-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling Reaction at Room Temperature
rationale: The article describes a copper-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between thioamides and arylboronic acids to form S-aryl thioimidates, which is a C-S bond-forming reaction. The catalyst is copper(II) acetate used as a soluble salt in solution (homogeneous), with no ligand specified in the optimized conditions (DBU is a base, not a ligand).

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Site-Selective C-H Sulfonylation via Aryl Thianthrenium Salts to Access Diarylsulfones
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed C(sp2)-S cross-coupling reaction between aryl thianthrenium salts and sodium sulfinates to form diarylsulfones. The catalyst system uses Pd2(dba)3 with XantPhos ligand in THF solution, which is homogeneous. The bond formed is C-S, which is not one of the specified C-C, C-O, or C-N coupling types.

title: Cascade Pd-Catalyzed Azide-Isocyanide Cross Coupling/Cyclization/Lactamization Reactions for the Synthesis of Tricyclic Guanidine-Containing Polyheterocycles
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed azide-isocyanide cross-coupling reaction, which forms C-N bonds as part of a cascade sequence to synthesize tricyclic guanidines. The catalysts used (Pd(OAc)2, Pd(PPh3)2Cl2, Pd(PPh3)4, Pd2(dba)3, etc.) are soluble molecular complexes operating in THF and other organic solvents, indicating homogeneous catalysis. The reaction is a metal-catalyzed coupling transformation.

title: Visible Light Photoredox-Catalyzed Radical Defluorinative Arylation of α-Trifluoromethyl Alkenes with Aryl Chlorides
rationale: The article describes a photoredox-catalyzed radical defluorinative arylation forming a C-C bond between α-trifluoromethyl alkenes and aryl chlorides. The catalyst is an organic photocatalyst (4CzIPN, eosin Y, etc.) operating in solution, making it homogeneous. No transition metal catalyst is used.

title: I2-Induced Metal-Free C(sp2)-H Functionalization of Indoles via One-Pot and Two-Step Reaction with 1-(2-Hydroxyphenyl)-propargyl Alcohols: Access to 3-(Benzofuran-3-yl)-1H-indoles
rationale: I2-catalyzed cross-coupling of indoles with propargyl alcohols to form C-C bonds, described as a metal-free, homogeneous process.

title: Merging of Two Photoredox Cycles with One Perovskite Catalyst Achieving Dual Functionalization: N-Heterocyclization and Site-Selective Bromination of N-Arylamines
rationale: The article describes a heterogeneous perovskite nanocrystal (CsPbBr3) photocatalytic system that drives N-heterocyclization of N-arylamines to form indoles, which involves C-N bond formation. The catalyst is a solid perovskite material (CsPbBr3 nanocrystals) operating in a different phase from reactants, making it heterogeneous. No transition metal is used for the catalytic bond formation (CsPbBr3 is a lead halide perovskite). The support category is 'Others' as perovskite materials don't fit standard support categories. The transformation involves C-N bond formation in the indole cyclization.

title: Difunctionalization of Alkenes toward 3,3-Disubstituted and Dihydrobenzoindolines by Using an Imidazolylidene Palladacyclic Catalyst
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed domino intramolecular cyclization/Sonogashira coupling reaction (a type of C-C bond-forming coupling) using a soluble imidazolylidene palladacyclic catalyst (IPr-Pdcycle-OxaNaphthyl). The catalyst is a molecular complex operating in solution, making it homogeneous.

title: Cu-Catalyzed Synthesis of Symmetric Diarylamines from Organoboronic Acids Using NaNO2 as the Amino Source
rationale: The article describes a copper-catalyzed synthesis of symmetric diarylamines from aryl boronic acids and NaNO2, forming C-N bonds. The catalyst is CuCl (and other copper salts) used in solution without any solid support, making it homogeneous. The system is explicitly described as 'ligand- and base-free', so ligand_name is null.

title: Synthesis of Polyfluorinated Biaryls via Palladium-Catalyzed Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling of Zinc Polyfluorobenzoates with Aryl Fluorosulfates
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed decarboxylative cross-coupling reaction between zinc polyfluorobenzoates and aryl fluorosulfates to form polyfluorinated biaryls (C-C bond formation). The catalyst used is Pd(PPh3)4 or PdCl2(PPh3)2, which are soluble molecular complexes operating in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis. The key ligand is triphenylphosphine (PPh3).

title: Access to Terminal Alkynes via Palladium-Catalyzed Coupling of ArCl with a Low Catalyst Loading of 0.08 mol %
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed Heck-Cassar reaction (a variant of Sonogashira coupling) between aryl chlorides and (triisopropylsilyl)acetylene to form C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (Pd(OAc)2 with XPhos ligand, or preformed XPhos-Pd-G1), operating in homogeneous conditions. The ligand XPhos is explicitly mentioned as key. The product is an alkyne, which after desilylation gives terminal alkynes.

title: One-Pot Synthesis of Benzoxazoles and Sulfoxides: Complete Utilization of Diaryl Sulfoxides
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between diaryl sulfoxides and benzoxazoles, forming C-C bonds (2-aryl benzoxazoles). The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex ([Pd(allyl)Cl]₂ with IPr·HCl ligand) operating in solution, making it homogeneous.

title: Copper-Catalyzed Deoxygenative C-N Coupling of Epoxides and Sulfonamides
rationale: The article describes a copper-catalyzed deoxygenative cross-coupling between epoxides and sulfonamides to form N-vinylsulfonamides, which is a C-N bond-forming reaction. The catalyst is a soluble copper salt (Cu(OTf)₂, Cu(OAc)₂, etc.) used in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis. No solid support or specific ligand is mentioned in the provided text.

title: Cross-Dimerization Giving Silyl-Substituted Conjugated Hexatrienes: An Approach to 1,6-Diarylhexa-1,3,5-trienes
rationale: The article describes two sequential catalytic coupling reactions: 1) Ru(0)-catalyzed cross-dimerization of alkynes with dienes to form silylated hexatrienes (C-C bond formation), and 2) Pd-catalyzed Hiyama cross-coupling of silylated intermediates with aryl iodides to form diarylhexatrienes (C-C bond formation). Both catalysts are soluble molecular complexes ([Ru(η⁶-naphthalene)(η⁴-1,5-cyclooctadiene)] and [Pd₂(dibenzylideneacetone)₃]), indicating homogeneous catalysis.

title: Mn(acac)3/Hydrazide-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidative Cross-Dehydrogenative Couplings of 1,2,3,4-Tetrahydroisoquinolines and Their Mechanistic Studies
rationale: The article describes a Mn(acac)3-catalyzed aerobic oxidative cross-dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) reaction between tetrahydroisoquinolines and various nucleophiles (nitroalkanes, malonates, etc.) to form C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (Mn(acac)3) operating in homogeneous phase with acac as the ligand.

title: Rh(III)-Catalyzed Fabrication of [4,3,1]-Bridged Azaheterocycles using Quinone Monoacetals
rationale: Rh(III)-catalyzed annulation via C-H activation and Michael addition forms C-C bonds. Catalyst [Cp*RhCl2]2 is a soluble molecular complex with Cp* ligand, operating homogeneously in solution.

title: Total Synthesis of (+)-Ansatrienol K
rationale: The abstract describes 'two sequential palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions' for constructing a benzene ring, which is a classic C-C bond-forming coupling process. The catalyst is a soluble Pd complex, indicating homogeneous catalysis. The specific ligand is not mentioned.

title: Total Synthesis of a Few Naturally Occurring Isocoumarins and Dihydroisocoumarins: Successful Exploration of the Ag(I)-Mediated 6-Endo-Dig Cyclization and Asymmetric Hydrogenation Strategy
rationale: The article describes multiple catalytic coupling reactions: 1) Sonogashira cross-coupling (Pd-catalyzed C-C bond formation) to access 2-alkynylated benzoates, 2) Ag(I)-mediated 6-endo-dig cyclization (C-O bond formation via lactonization), and 3) Ru-BINAP catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation (not a coupling reaction). The Sonogashira coupling is a classic C-C bond forming reaction using homogeneous Pd catalysis. The Ag-mediated cyclization forms C-O bonds but is not a traditional coupling reaction; however, the Sonogashira qualifies it as relevant. The catalysts are all soluble molecular complexes (Pd, Ag salts, Ru-BINAP complex), making them homogeneous. BINAP is specified as the ligand for Ru in hydrogenation, but no ligand is specified for Pd in Sonogashira. The primary coupling type is C-C from Sonogashira.

title: Cooperative Ruthenium/Amine Catalysis of the Cross-Coupling of Ketones as Alkenyl Electrophiles
rationale: The article describes a cooperative Ru/amine catalytic system for cross-coupling of ketones with organoboron compounds to form C(sp2)-C(sp2) bonds. The catalyst is Ru3(CO)12, a soluble molecular complex operating in solution, making it homogeneous. No solid support is involved. The amine (pyrrolidine) acts as a cooperative catalyst/transient leaving group but is not a ligand coordinated to Ru, so ligand_name is null. The bond formed is C-C.

title: Silver- and Base-Enabled SOMOphilic Alkynylation of Alkylboronic Acids with Bromoalkynes
rationale: The article describes a silver-catalyzed (AgOTf) SOMOphilic alkynylation reaction forming C(sp)-C(sp3) bonds between alkylboronic acids and bromoalkynes. The catalyst is a soluble silver salt (AgOTf) used in stoichiometric or catalytic amounts with base (Cs2CO3) in DCE solvent, indicating homogeneous catalysis. No solid support is involved, and no specific ligand is mentioned for silver.

title: Blue-Light-Irradiated Copper-Catalyzed Regio-tunable Double C-H/C-H Cross-Coupling Reaction: A Sustainable Approach to Construct C2-Indolyl-1,4-naphthoquinones
rationale: The article describes a copper-catalyzed double C-H/C-H cross-coupling reaction between 1,4-naphthoquinone and indole under blue-light irradiation, forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is CuCl2·2H2O, a soluble copper salt used in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis. No solid support or specific ligand is mentioned.

title: Precise Synthesis of Ester-Functionalized Cyclo[6]- and Cyclo[7]furans
rationale: The article describes a Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction using tris(dibenzylideneacetone)dipalladium(0) and tri-tert-butylphosphonium tetrafluoroborate as a soluble catalyst-ligand system, forming C-C bonds to synthesize cyclo[n]furan macrocycles.

title: Total Synthesis of Labile Antibacterial Polyketide Thailandamide A and a More Stable but Equally Potent Morpholine Amide Derivative
rationale: The article describes a total synthesis using Negishi and Heck coupling reactions as pivotal steps. Table 1 explicitly details homogeneous Pd catalysts (PdCl2(MeCN)2, Pd(PPh3)4, PdCl2(PPh3)2, Pd(OAc)2, [Pd(μ-I)(PtBu3)]2) for Heck coupling, forming C-C bonds. The catalysts are molecular complexes in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Ring-Opening Defluorinative Hiyama Cross-Coupling of gem-Difluorocyclopropanes with Arylsilanes
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed Hiyama cross-coupling reaction between gem-difluorocyclopropanes and arylsilanes to form C-C bonds. The catalyst is Pd(OAc)2 with phosphine ligands (DavePhos, JohnPhos, XantPhos, RuPhos, P(Cy)3) in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis. The reaction forms C-C bonds via ring-opening defluorinative coupling.

title: Zn(OTf)2-Catalyzed and HFIP-Assisted Synthesis of Benzo[b]acridine-6,11-diones via C-H Functionalization of Naphthoquinone
rationale: The article describes a Zn(OTf)2-catalyzed synthesis of benzo[b]acridine-6,11-diones from naphthoquinone and 2-carbonyl-anilines via C-H functionalization and annulation. This is a catalytic coupling reaction forming both C-C and C-N bonds (cyclization to form azaanthraquinone core). The catalyst is a soluble Zn salt (Zn(OTf)2) in organic solvent, making it homogeneous. No ligand is specified, and no solid support is involved.

title: Cu-Catalyzed Acylation of Quinoline-N-oxides with gem-Difluorostyrenes via the Tandem Cycloaddition/Elimination/Oxidation Process
rationale: The article describes a copper-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between quinoline-N-oxides and gem-difluorostyrenes to form 2-aroylquinolines, which involves C-C bond formation. The catalyst is a soluble copper salt (CuBr, CuCl, etc.) used in DMF solvent, indicating homogeneous catalysis. No solid support or specific ligand is mentioned.

title: Regioselective Modification Distinguishing Slight Difference between Two C-Br Bonds in 1,7-Dibromonaphthalene and Synthesis of Unsymmetric Naphthalene Derivatives
rationale: The article describes Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions (C-C bond formation) using soluble Pd complexes (Pd(OAc)2/BINAP and Pd(PPh3)4) in solution, which is homogeneous catalysis. The main catalytic system optimized is Pd(PPh3)4, indicating a homogeneous Pd complex with PPh3 ligands.

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling of 2,4-Dienoic Acids and Aryl Halides: Access to Fluorescence Active (E,E)-1,4-Diarylbutadienes
rationale: Pd-catalyzed decarboxylative cross-coupling of 2,4-dienoic acids with aryl halides to form C-C bonds. The catalyst system uses PdCl2 with PPh3 ligand in solution (DMA/DMF), indicating homogeneous catalysis. Silver salt is used as a cocatalyst/additive, not as the primary catalytic metal.

title: Visible-Light-Induced Nickel/Organoboron Dual Catalysis for the Synthesis of Primary Aryl Amines
rationale: The article describes a visible-light-induced Ni/photoredox dual catalytic system for the cross-coupling of aryl bromides with trimethylsilyl azide to form primary aryl amines (C-N bonds). The catalyst is a soluble NiCl2·DME complex with dtbbpy ligand, operating homogeneously in solution alongside a molecular organoboron photocatalyst (AQDAB).

title: Photoinduced Cobaloxime Catalysis for Oxidant-Free Radical Cyclization of 2-Methylthiolated Alkynones to Access Phosphorylated Thiochromones
rationale: The article describes a photoinduced cobaloxime-catalyzed radical phosphinylation/cyclization reaction that forms a C-C bond between an alkynone and a phosphine oxide to create a phosphorylated thiochromone. The catalyst is a soluble molecular cobaloxime complex (Co(dmgH)₂pyCl derivatives), making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Synthesis of Biaryl-Based Phosphasilinanes via Giese-Type Addition for Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling Reactions
rationale: Article describes Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions (Buchwald-Hartwig and Suzuki-Miyaura) forming C-N and C-C bonds using soluble molecular Pd complexes with newly developed phosphasilinane-based ligands. Table 1 explicitly shows yields for both C-N and C-C coupling reactions.

title: Mechanistic Basis for Divergent Stereoselectivity in Intramolecular Ni-Catalyzed Cross-Electrophile Coupling Reactions
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling (XEC) reaction, specifically a Negishi-type coupling forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble nickel complex operating in solution (homogeneous), as evidenced by mechanistic studies of organonickel intermediates and chiral nickel catalysts. No solid support is mentioned, and while a ligand is implied for asymmetric control, none is specified in the provided text.

title: Cooperative Ni/Vitamin B12-Catalyzed Hydroarylation of Styrene Derivatives with Aryl Iodides
rationale: The article describes a cooperative Ni/Vitamin B12-catalyzed hydroarylation of styrenes with aryl iodides, forming C-C bonds. Vitamin B12 is a cobalt-containing complex, making this a bimetallic Ni/Co homogeneous catalytic system operating in solution. The reaction is a coupling transformation (hydroarylation) that creates new C-C bonds between aryl and alkene carbons.

title: Microwave-Assisted Intramolecular Dehydrogenative Coupling Reaction: Access to γ-Carboline Derivatives
rationale: The article describes a Pd(II)/Cu(II)-catalyzed intramolecular dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) reaction forming C-C bonds to construct γ-carboline derivatives. The catalysts (Pd(OAc)2, Cu(OAc)2) are soluble metal salts used in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis. No solid support is mentioned, and the ligand field is left blank as no specific ligand is emphasized in the optimal conditions (Pd(OAc)2 + Cu(OAc)2).

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Denitrative Mizoroki-Heck Reaction of Nitroarenes and Buta-1,3-dienes
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed denitrative Mizoroki-Heck reaction, which is a C-C bond-forming coupling reaction. The catalyst system uses Pd(acac)2 with BrettPhos ligand in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis.

title: Synthetic, Computational, and Experimental Studies of a Class 3 Atropisomeric α-Naphthyl Tropone
rationale: The article describes an 'atropselective Suzuki cross-coupling' for asymmetric synthesis. Suzuki coupling is a Pd-catalyzed C-C bond forming reaction. The catalyst is not specified as a solid material, and the reaction is performed in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis. No specific ligand is mentioned in the provided text.

title: Development of a Scalable Synthesis of a HPK1 Inhibitor Featuring a Direct α-Arylation of Boc-Protected N,N-Dimethylamine by Palladium-Mediated Negishi Cross-Coupling
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed Negishi cross-coupling reaction (a classic C-C bond-forming coupling) for the synthesis of a pharmaceutical intermediate. The catalyst system uses Pd with DPPF ligand in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis. The metallaphotoredox approach mentioned uses Ni complexes with ligands like dtbbpy and L1, but the optimized scalable route is the Pd/DPPF-catalyzed Negishi coupling.

title: All-E-Carotenoid Synthesis via Suzuki Coupling of α,ω-Dibromopentaene: HPLC Optimization of the Catalytic Reaction Conditions
rationale: The article describes a Suzuki coupling reaction forming C-C bonds using soluble Pd complexes with phosphine ligands (Pd(PPh3)4, Pd(OAc)2/2PPh3, Pd(PPh3)2Cl2, Pd(dppf)Cl2, Pd(t-Bu3P)2) in solution, which is homogeneous catalysis.

title: Pd-Catalyzed One-Pot Synthesis of Indole-3-carboxylic Acids via a Sequential Water-Mediated Nucleophilic Addition to Amides/Esters and Carbon-Heteroatom Cross-Coupling Reaction Strategy
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed one-pot synthesis involving a Buchwald-Hartwig amination step, which is a C-N bond-forming coupling reaction. The catalyst is PdCl2 or Pd(PPh3)4 used in solution with phosphine ligands (PPh3, MePhos, DPEphos, bpy tested), indicating homogeneous catalysis. The key transformation forms a C-N bond via amination.

title: Unifying Electric Field Catalysis with the Inductive Effect, Electro-Inductive Effect, and Differential Solvation-Induced Catalysis
rationale: The article uses the oxidative addition step of Suzuki-Miyaura coupling as the model reaction to study electric field effects. This is a Pd-catalyzed C-C bond forming coupling reaction. The catalyst is described as Pd(0) in the oxidative addition step, which is a homogeneous molecular catalyst (no solid support mentioned).

title: Decarbonylative/Acylative Sonogashira Coupling of Biomass-Derived Furandicarbonyl Dichloride: A Route to Unsymmetrically Disubstituted Furans
rationale: The article describes a Cu/Pd-catalyzed decarbonylative/acylative Sonogashira cross-coupling reaction between furandicarbonyl dichloride and terminal alkynes to form C-C bonds. The catalyst system uses soluble Pd salts (PdCl2, Pd(OAc)2, etc.) with phosphine ligands (Xantphos, XPhos, etc.) and a Cu co-catalyst in THF solvent, indicating homogeneous catalysis.

title: Theoretical Study on an Excited-State Copper-Catalyzed [4 + 1] Cyclization Reaction for the Construction of α,β-Unsaturated-γ-Lactams via an Oxidative Radical-Polar Crossover Mechanism
rationale: The article describes an excited-state copper-catalyzed [4+1] cyclization reaction forming α,β-unsaturated-γ-lactams via C-C bond formation (radical relay) and C-N bond formation (ring closure). The catalyst is a soluble Cu(I)-BINAP complex operating homogeneously in solution.

title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Cross-Electrophile Dehydroxylative and Desulfonylative Allylation
rationale: The article describes a cobalt-catalyzed cross-electrophile dehydroxylative allylation reaction forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is CoBr2 with a bipyridine ligand (L1) in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Electrochemically Oxidative C-H/N-H Cross-Coupling Reactions of Sulfoximines with Imidazopyridines
rationale: Electrochemical oxidative C-H/N-H cross-coupling between sulfoximines and imidazopyridines forms C-N bonds. The abstract explicitly states 'in the absence of exogenous oxidants and metal catalysts,' and the optimization table shows no metal catalyst is used. The reaction is mediated electrochemically with n-Bu4NI as a supporting salt/mediator in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Catalyst, Base, Additives, and Solvent: The Tools to Dig a Better CANAL Reaction
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed Catalytic Arene Norbornene Annulation (CANAL) reaction, which is a coupling reaction forming C-C bonds. The catalyst system uses soluble Pd with phosphine ligands (SPhos, XPhos) in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Diazo Strategy for the Synthesis of Functionalized Naphtho[2,1-d]oxazoles
rationale: The article describes a Rh(II)-catalyzed transformation involving formal insertion of a metallocarbene into an aromatic C-H bond to form a new C-C bond, constructing the naphtho[2,1-d]oxazole core. This is a metal-catalyzed coupling reaction (C-H functionalization/carbene insertion). The catalyst is a soluble Rh(II) complex (homogeneous). The abstract also mentions subsequent Sonogashira cross-coupling, but the primary catalytic transformation described is the Rh-catalyzed C-H insertion.

title: Three-Phase Emulsions during Cross-Coupling Reactions in Water
rationale: The article studies a palladium-catalyzed Suzuki cross-coupling reaction (C-C bond formation) in aqueous surfactant systems. The catalyst is palladium acetate with SPhos ligand, forming a soluble molecular complex in the reaction medium, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Second-Generation Catalyst System for Ag-Mediated Liebeskind-Srogl Coupling of Tetrazine Thioethers with Arylboronic Acids
rationale: The article describes a PdI2/DiPPF catalyst system for silver-mediated Liebeskind-Srogl coupling of tetrazine thioethers with arylboronic acids, forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (Pd salt with phosphine ligand), making it homogeneous.

title: Photoinduced Cross-Coupling Reactions of Diazoalkanes via a Selective Denitrogenation/Cyclization/Addition Cascade for Diversity-Oriented Synthesis of N-Acyl Pyrazolines
rationale: The article describes a photoinduced cross-coupling reaction of diazoalkanes forming N-acyl pyrazolines, which involves C-C bond formation (in pyrazoline ring) and C-N bond formation (N-acylation). The protocol explicitly states it is 'free of photocatalysts' and uses only visible light irradiation with a small amount of Et3N as additive, indicating a homogeneous, metal-free process.

title: Activation of gem-Dichloroacetamides and Epoxides Using Elemental Sulfur and Amines: A Route to Monothiooxalamides and α-Ketothioamides
rationale: The main focus is on metal-free synthesis of monothiooxalamides via C-S/C-N bond formation. However, the article explicitly states that ligand studies revealed monothiooxalamides exhibit high efficacy as ligands in Cu-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling reactions. This qualifies as a catalyst-mediated coupling reaction forming C-N bonds using a homogeneous Cu catalyst with monothiooxalamide ligands.

title: Electrochemically Driven Nickel-Catalyzed Synthesis of Aryl Alkyl Ketones by the Cross-Coupling of Carboxylic Esters with Alkylpyridinium Salts
rationale: The article describes an electrochemical Ni-catalyzed reductive cross-coupling of arylcarboxylic esters with alkylpyridinium salts to form aryl alkyl ketones (C-C bond formation). The catalyst is a soluble Ni complex (Ni(dme)Br2) with ligand L1 (bipyridine-type ligand mentioned in optimization table), operating in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Heteroannulation of Bdan-Capped Alkynes: Rapid Access to Complex Indole Scaffolds
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed heteroannulation (a type of C-C bond-forming coupling) between 2-iodoaniline derivatives and alkynes to form indoles. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (Pd(dppf)Cl2 or Pd(OAc)2 with dppf ligand), indicating homogeneous catalysis. The ligand dppf is explicitly mentioned in the table.

The catalysts are soluble metal complexes (Ni and Cu) operating in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Enantioselective nickel-catalysed electrochemical cross-dehydrogenative amination
rationale: Article describes nickel-catalyzed electrochemical cross-dehydrogenative amination forming C(sp3)-N bonds. The catalyst is NiCl2 with chiral diamine ligands (L8, L7, L6) in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis. The reaction is a coupling between acylimidazoles and nitrogen nucleophiles to form C-N bonds.

title: Suzuki-Miyaura coupling of arylthianthrenium tetrafluoroborate salts under acidic conditions
rationale: Article describes a palladium-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling (SMC) reaction forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is described as 'palladium-catalysed' and references to 'Pd-XPhos precatalyst' and 'intermediate arylpalladium(II) complex' indicate a homogeneous molecular palladium catalyst system. No solid support is mentioned, and the reaction occurs in solution under acidic conditions.

title: Enantioselective alkyl-alkyl coupling by Ni-catalysed asymmetric cross-hydrodimerization of alkenes
rationale: The article describes a Ni-catalyzed asymmetric cross-hydrodimerization of alkenes to form alkyl-alkyl (C(sp3)-C(sp3)) bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (Ni with chiral ligands like L1-L6) operating in solution, making it homogeneous. The reaction is a coupling process forming C-C bonds.

title: Copper-catalysed synthesis of chiral alkynyl cyclopropanes using enantioconvergent radical cross-coupling of cyclopropyl halides with terminal alkynes
rationale: The article describes a copper-catalyzed enantioconvergent radical cross-coupling between cyclopropyl halides and terminal alkynes to form C-C bonds. The catalyst system uses Cu(II) salts (e.g., Cu(OAc)2, Cu(OTf)2) with hard chiral N,N,N-ligands in solution, which is characteristic of homogeneous catalysis.

title: Iron-catalysed radical Markovnikov hydroamidation of complex alkenes
rationale: The article describes an iron-catalyzed radical Markovnikov hydroamidation of alkenes using Fe(acac)₃ (iron acetylacetonate) as a soluble catalyst, forming C-N bonds via a coupling reaction between alkenes and a cyanamide reagent.

title: Iron-catalysed direct coupling of organosodium compounds
rationale: The article describes iron-catalyzed oxidative homocoupling and cross-coupling reactions using organosodium compounds to form C(sp2)-C(sp2) and C(sp2)-C(sp3) bonds. The catalyst is an iron complex in solution (FeCl2 with TMEDA additive), operating homogeneously. No solid support is involved, and while TMEDA acts as a coordinating additive, it is not a traditional ligand in the organometallic sense but rather a Lewis donor controlling reactivity.

title: Applying alternating current in paired photo-electrocatalysis for asymmetric cross-coupling of alcohols
rationale: The article describes an enantioselective C(sp3)-C(sp2) cross-coupling of alcohols using asymmetric nickel catalysis with bipyridine ligands, integrated with photo-electrocatalysis. This is a homogeneous catalytic system (soluble nickel complex) performing a C-C bond-forming coupling reaction.

title: Nickel-catalysed enantioselective migratory reductive cross-coupling enabled by radical 1,2-amino migration
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed enantioselective migratory reductive cross-coupling reaction forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (NiBr₂·DME or similar with modified chiral Bilm ligands), operating homogeneously in solution.

title: Isolated carbon(I) species featuring a carbone cation radical
rationale: The article describes a carbon(I) radical cation species ([1-CDC]•+) that mediates C-O and C-C cross-coupling reactions with electron-deficient aryl halides. The catalyst is a molecular species (carbodicarbene-derived radical cation) operating in solution, making it homogeneous. No metal is involved; the catalytic center is carbon. The ligand framework includes N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligands.

title: Visible-light-induced C(sp3)-C(sp3) bond formation via radical/radical cross-coupling
rationale: The article describes a visible-light-induced radical/radical cross-coupling reaction forming C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds, which is a C-C coupling. The catalyst is fac-Ir(ppy)3, a soluble molecular photocatalyst, indicating homogeneous catalysis. The metal is Ir, and the ligand is ppy (2-phenylpyridine).

title: Nickel-catalyzed sulfonylative coupling of 2-chlorobenzothiazoles with sulfinates at room temperature
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between 2-chlorobenzothiazoles and sodium sulfinates to form C-S bonds (sulfonylative coupling). The catalyst is a soluble Ni(OTf)2 salt with ligand L1 (homogeneous system).

title: The molecular-level effect of alkoxide additives in iron-catalyzed Kumada cross-coupling with simple ferric salts
rationale: The article investigates iron-catalyzed Kumada cross-coupling reactions using simple ferric salts (Fe(acac)₃) in solution, forming C-C bonds between alkyl Grignards and alkenyl/aryl halides. The catalyst is a soluble iron salt, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Visible-light induced metal-free intramolecular reductive cyclisations of ketones with alkynes and allenes
rationale: The article describes a visible-light-induced intramolecular reductive cyclization of ketones with alkynes/allenes forming C-O bonds via ketyl radical hydroalkoxylation. The catalyst is 4-CzIPN (an organic photocatalyst), making it metal-free homogeneous catalysis.

title: Visible-light-absorbing C-N cross-coupling for the synthesis of hydrazones involving C(sp2)-H/C(sp3)-H functionalization
rationale: The article describes a visible-light-mediated C-N cross-coupling reaction for hydrazone synthesis using the organic photocatalyst eosin Y. The method is explicitly metal-free, uses a soluble organic dye (eosin Y) as the photocatalyst, and forms C-N bonds via C-H functionalization.

title: Enantioselective reductive allylic alkylation enabled by dual photoredox/palladium catalysis
rationale: The article describes a dual photoredox/palladium catalyzed reductive cross-coupling of allylic acetates with alkyl bromides to form C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds. The catalyst is described as a 'chiral Pd complex' operating in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis. While the abstract mentions enantioselectivity control by a chiral Pd complex, the specific ligand name is not provided in the given text.

title: Investigating the mechanism and origins of selectivity in palladium-catalysed carbene insertion cross-coupling reactions
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed carbene insertion cross-coupling reaction forming C-C bonds (tri-substituted alkenes). The catalyst is a soluble Pd/PPh3 complex operating in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis.

title: Computational mechanistic analysis of a cationic Suzuki-Miyaura reaction without added base
rationale: The article describes a computational mechanistic study of a base-free Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction, which forms C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble Pd complex with phosphine ligands, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Theoretical investigation of mechanism on nickel-catalyzed electrochemical cross-coupling of aryl bromides and arylamines
rationale: The article describes a theoretical study of a nickel-catalyzed electrochemical cross-coupling reaction between aryl bromides and arylamines, forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular nickel complex with bipyridine or tridentate ligands, operating in a homogeneous phase.

title: Easy preparation of small crystalline Pd2Sn nanoparticles in solution at room temperature
rationale: The article describes Pd2Sn nanoparticles (bimetallic alloy NPs) used as nanocatalysts in solution for Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling, which forms C-C bonds. The catalyst is solid nanoparticles operating in a different phase from reactants (heterogeneous). The support category is 'Metals' as it's a bimetallic alloy nanoparticle system.

title: A theoretical study of the ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed regiodivergent synthesis of dibenzosilepin derivatives
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization forming C-C bonds via alkyne insertion and reductive elimination. The catalyst is Pd(OAc)2 with BINAP ligand in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: A naphthalene-based heterobimetallic triazolylidene IrIII/PdII complex: regioselective to regiospecific C-H activation, tandem catalysis and a copper-free Sonogashira reaction
rationale: The article describes a heterobimetallic Ir/Pd complex used as a pre-catalyst in tandem Suzuki-Miyaura/transfer hydrogenation and as a catalyst in Sonogashira coupling and α-arylation reactions, all of which are C-C bond-forming coupling reactions. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (homogeneous) with a triazolylidene ligand.

title: Steric and electronic effects of arsa-Buchwald ligands on Suzuki-Miyaura coupling reaction
rationale: The article explicitly studies Suzuki-Miyaura coupling (SMC), a classic C-C bond-forming cross-coupling reaction. It focuses on arsa-Buchwald ligands (arsenic analogs of Buchwald ligands) used with palladium, forming soluble molecular complexes in solution, which is characteristic of homogeneous catalysis.

title: Novel 1,2,3-triazolyl phosphine with a pyridyl functionality: synthesis, coinage metal complexes, photophysical studies and Cu(I) catalyzed C-O coupling of phenols with aryl bromides
rationale: The article describes Cu(I) complexes (specifically complex 4) catalyzing C-O coupling of phenols with aryl bromides (Ullmann-type reaction) under mild conditions. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex, making it homogeneous. The ligand is a synthesized 1,2,3-triazolyl phosphine with a pyridyl functionality.

title: Copper-catalyzed direct synthesis of 3-methylene-2-arylisoindolin-1-ones with calcium carbide as a surrogate of gaseous acetylene
rationale: The article describes a copper-catalyzed Sonogashira cross-coupling reaction forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble copper salt (CuI, Cu(OAc)2, CuOTf) used in solution, making it homogeneous. No solid support is involved, and no specific ligand is mentioned in the optimization table or abstract, so ligand_name is null.

title: Metal-free and site-selective α-C-H functionalization of tetrahydrofuran enabled by the photocatalytic generation of bromine radicals
rationale: The article describes a metal-free photocatalytic system using 4-CzIPN as photocatalyst and nBu4NBr as cocatalyst for C-H functionalization of THF to form C-S and C-C bonds through cross-coupling reactions. The system is homogeneous (soluble photocatalyst and cocatalyst) and explicitly states 'transition-metal free'.

title: Current-controlled nickel-catalyzed multi-electrophile electroreductive cross-coupling
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed electroreductive cross-electrophile coupling (carbonylative coupling) forming alkyl aryl ketones (C-C bonds) from alkyl halides, aryl iodides, and propyl chloroformate. The catalyst is NiCl2·dme with dtbpy ligand, operating in solution (homogeneous).

title: Metal-free acceptorless dehydrogenative cross-coupling of aldehydes/alcohols with alcohols
rationale: The article describes a metal-free photocatalytic dehydrogenative cross-coupling of aldehydes/alcohols with alcohols to form esters (C-O bonds). The catalytic system uses organophotocatalyst 4CzIPN and thiol HAT catalysts in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis without transition metals.

title: Dual ligand approach increases functional group tolerance in the Pd-catalysed C-H arylation of N-heterocyclic pharmaceuticals
rationale: Pd-catalyzed C-H arylation (a C-C bond-forming coupling reaction) using a dual ligand approach with phosphine and 2-hydroxypyridine ligands in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis.

title: Sodium-iodide-promoted nickel-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling of aryl chlorides and N-nucleophiles under visible-light irradiation
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling reaction between aryl chlorides/bromides and N-nucleophiles under visible-light irradiation. The catalyst system uses Ni(COD)₂ with dtbbpy (4,4′-di-tert-butyl-2,2′-bipyridine) ligand in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis. Sodium iodide acts as a promoter, not as a support.

title: Semi-heterogeneous g-C3N4/NaI dual catalytic C-C bond formation under visible light
rationale: The article describes a C-C bond formation reaction between quinoxalin-2(1H)-ones and arylhydrazines using a dual catalytic system with g-C3N4 as a heterogeneous photocatalyst and NaI as a homogeneous redox catalyst. The primary catalytic component for the coupling is the solid g-C3N4 material, which is a nitride-based photocatalyst. No metal catalyst is used; the iodide salt (NaI) acts as a redox mediator. The bond formed is C-C.

title: Heterocyclic Suzuki-Miyaura coupling reaction of metalla-aromatics and mechanistic analysis of site selectivity
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction, which is a classic C-C bond-forming coupling. The catalyst used is Pd2(dba)3 (a soluble molecular complex) with optimization trials including Pd(PPh3)4, Pd(dba)2, and Pd(OAc)2, all homogeneous catalysts. No solid support is mentioned, confirming homogeneous catalysis.

title: Mechanochemical solid state single electron transfer from reduced organic hydrocarbon for catalytic aryl-halide bond activation
rationale: The article describes a mechanochemical solid-state catalytic system using phenalenyl anion as an organic electron donor for aryl-halide bond activation and subsequent C-C cross-coupling reactions. The catalyst operates in solid state under ball milling conditions, making it heterogeneous. No transition metal is used (transition metal-free conditions), and the solid-state organic hydrocarbon catalyst falls under 'Others' support category.

title: A cheap metal catalyzed ring expansion/cross-coupling cascade: a new route to functionalized medium-sized and macrolactones
rationale: The article describes a Cu-catalyzed ring expansion/cross-coupling cascade forming medium-sized and macrolactones. The abstract explicitly mentions 'cheap metal catalysis' and 'cross-coupling cascade', with DFT calculations proposing a Cu(I)/Cu(II)/Cu(III) catalytic cycle. The catalyst is a soluble copper species (no solid support mentioned), making it homogeneous. The cross-coupling step forms C-C bonds (cycloalkyl-Cu(III) species undergoes reductive elimination).

title: Encapsulated C12A7 electride material enables a multistep electron transfer process for cross-coupling reactions
rationale: The article describes a composite catalytic system (Pd/Gr/C12A7:e−) for Suzuki coupling reactions, which is a C-C bond forming cross-coupling. The catalyst consists of Pd nanoparticles supported on graphene (Gr) and C12A7 electride, making it a heterogeneous solid catalyst. The support is primarily graphene, which falls under the 'Carbon' category.

title: Three-component reductive conjugate addition/aldol tandem reaction enabled by nickel/photoredox dual catalysis
rationale: The article describes a nickel/photoredox dual-catalyzed three-component reductive cross-coupling of aryl halides, aldehydes, and alkenes to form C-C bonds. The catalyst system uses soluble Ni salts (e.g., NiBr2·DME) and a ligand (L2) in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis. The photoredox catalyst (e.g., Ir(ppy)3) is also molecular and soluble. The reaction is a reductive conjugate addition/aldol tandem sequence, which is a C-C bond-forming coupling.

title: NIS-initiated photo-induced oxidative decarboxylative sulfoximidation of cinnamic acids
rationale: The article describes a photo-induced oxidative decarboxylative cross-coupling between cinnamic acids and NH-sulfoximines, forming a C-N bond. The catalyst is N-Iodosuccinimide (NIS), an organic iodine compound, which operates homogeneously in solution. No metal catalyst is used.

title: A novel strategy of constructing an artificial light-harvesting system based on a supramolecular organic framework for photocatalysis
rationale: The article describes a supramolecular organic framework (SOF)-based light-harvesting system used as a catalyst for an aerobic cross-dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) reaction, which is a C-C bond-forming coupling reaction. The catalyst is a solid supramolecular assembly (SOF) operating in aqueous solution, making it heterogeneous. No metal catalyst is used; the catalysis is based on organic components and energy transfer. The SOF is classified as 'Others' for support as it is a supramolecular organic framework not fitting other categories.

title: Regioselective coupling of benzyl chlorides with allyl and allenyl boronates catalysed by a bidentate phosphine ligand/palladium catalyst
rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura coupling reaction between benzyl chlorides and allyl/allenyl boronates to form C-C bonds. The catalyst system uses soluble Pd precursors (Pd(OAc)2, Pd2dba3, etc.) with bidentate phosphine ligands (Xantphos, BINAP, dppf, etc.) in organic solvents, indicating homogeneous catalysis. The key ligand identified in optimization is Xantphos.

title: Cu(I)-catalysed cross-coupling reaction of in situ generated azomethine ylides towards easy construction of fused N-heterocycles
rationale: CuI salt used as catalyst in solution for decarboxylative C-N coupling followed by C-C and C-S cyclization to form fused N-heterocycles. This is a homogeneous copper-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction forming both C-N and C-C bonds.

title: Regioselective synthesis of phenanthridine-fused quinazolinones using a 9-mesityl-10-methylacridinium perchlorate photocatalyst
rationale: The article describes a visible-light-induced intramolecular C-N cross-coupling reaction using 9-mesityl-10-methylacridinium perchlorate (Mes-Acr-MeClO4) as an organic photocatalyst. This is a metal-free, homogeneous photoredox-catalyzed coupling reaction forming C-N bonds.

title: Tandem Pd-catalyzed annulation/coupling of acetylenic enamines with aryl triflates
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed tandem annulation/coupling reaction forming two new C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble Pd complex (Pd(dba)2 with RuPhos ligand) operating in solution, making it homogeneous. The reaction involves cross-coupling as part of the cascade.

title: Copper-catalyzed umpolung Sonogashira-type coupling of arene boronic acids under visible light
rationale: Copper-catalyzed Sonogashira-type coupling of aryl/alkenyl boronic acids with alkynyl-1,2-benziodoxol-3(1H)-ones to form diaryl alkynes and enynes (C-C bond formation) under visible light. The catalyst is described as 'copper catalyst' without mention of solid support, indicating homogeneous conditions.

title: Organogelation enables fast organolithium cross-coupling reactions in air
rationale: Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling of organolithium reagents with aryl bromides (C-C bond formation) using soluble Pd complexes like Pd-PEPPSI-IPentCl and Pd[P(tBu)3]2, which are homogeneous catalysts.

title: Palladium-loaded ceramic membrane-catalyzed flow-through Suzuki-Miyaura reaction
rationale: Pd-loaded ceramic membrane used as a solid catalyst in a flow reactor for Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling, forming C-C bonds. Ceramic membranes are typically metal oxides (e.g., Al2O3, ZrO2).

title: Visible light/copper catalysis enabled alkylation of silyl enol ethers with arylsulfonium salts
rationale: The article describes a visible light/copper-catalyzed alkylation reaction forming C-C bonds between silyl enol ethers and arylsulfonium salts to produce aryl alkyl thioethers. The copper(I) photocatalyst operates in solution (homogeneous), and the transformation is a radical-mediated C-C coupling.

title: Aqueous mediated iodine catalyzed C-N coupling followed by C-C coupling towards 5H-pyrazino[2,3-b]indoles
rationale: Iodine-catalyzed oxidative cross-coupling reactions forming C-N bond followed by C-C bond via intramolecular cyclization to synthesize 5H-pyrazino[2,3-b]indoles. Catalyst is molecular iodine (I2) in aqueous solution, making it homogeneous catalysis with no metal involved.

title: Nickel-catalyzed stereoselective reductive cross-coupling of gem-difluoroalkenes with alkenyl electrophiles
rationale: The article describes a Ni-catalyzed defluorinative cross-electrophile coupling between gem-difluoroalkenes and alkenyl electrophiles to form C(sp2)-C(sp2) bonds. The catalyst system uses Ni(acac)2 with ligand L2 in solution (DMSO), making it homogeneous catalysis. The reaction forms C-C bonds specifically.

title: Perfluoroalkoxylation reaction via dual concurrent catalysis
rationale: The article describes a CsI-catalyzed perfluoroalkoxylation reaction forming C-O bonds between alkyl halides and perfluoroalkoxides. CsI is a soluble salt catalyst operating in homogeneous phase, forming C-O bonds via nucleophilic substitution.

title: Pd-catalyzed synthesis of hetero 1,2-interlinked C-disaccharides by coupling of iodo glycals with glycals
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed coupling reaction between iodo glycals and glycals to form C1-C2 interlinked disaccharides, which is a C-C bond forming reaction. The catalyst is Pd(OAc)2 with PPh3 ligand in DMF solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis. The optimization table shows Pd(OAc)2 with PPh3 ligand and AgOAc base giving best yields, confirming homogeneous Pd catalysis for C-C bond formation.

title: Non-directed Pd-catalysed C-H arylation of [2.2]paracyclophane
rationale: Pd-catalyzed C-H arylation of [2.2]paracyclophane with aryl iodides forms C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular Pd complex (Pd(PCy3)2Cl2) with phosphine ligands, operating in homogeneous conditions.

title: Tip-enhanced Raman imaging of plasmon-driven dimerization of 4-bromothiophenol on nickel-decorated gold nanoplate bimetallic nanostructures
rationale: The article describes plasmon-driven dimerization of 4-bromothiophenol into 4,4′-biphenyldithiol, which is a C-C coupling reaction. The reaction occurs on nickel-decorated gold nanoplate bimetallic nanostructures (Ni@AuNPs), making it heterogeneous catalysis using bimetallic nanoparticles.

title: Palladium-catalyzed coupling of amides and cyclopropanols for the synthesis of γ-diketones
rationale: Palladium-catalyzed coupling of amides and cyclopropanols to form γ-diketones through simultaneous C-N and C-C activation. The catalyst is described as a palladium catalytic method without mention of solid support, indicating homogeneous catalysis. The reaction forms C-C bonds between acyl and β-keto alkyl fragments.

title: Asymmetric alkene-alkene reductive cross-coupling reaction via visible-light photoredox/cobalt dual catalysis
rationale: The article describes an asymmetric alkene-alkene reductive cross-coupling reaction via visible-light photoredox/cobalt dual catalysis, forming C-C bonds. The catalyst system uses Co(OAc)2·4H2O with ligand L1 (a chiral ligand) in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Visible-light induced cross-electrophile coupling of imines and anhydrides to synthesize α-amino ketones
rationale: Visible-light mediated reductive cross-electrophile coupling of imines and anhydrides to form α-amino ketones (C-C bond formation). The reaction is photoredox catalyzed (likely organic photocatalyst) without metal catalyst, operating in solution phase.

title: A transition metal- and photosensitizer-free approach for site-selective (hetero)arylation of polychlorinated heteroarenes
rationale: The article describes a photochemical method for site-selective (hetero)arylation of polychlorinated heteroarenes, forming C-C bonds via C(sp2)-Cl/C(sp2)-H cross-coupling. The approach explicitly eliminates transition metal catalysts and photosensitizers, relying instead on in situ formation of electron donor-acceptor (EDA) complexes between substrates and a basic additive (Cs2CO3). This is a metal-free, homogeneous photochemical coupling reaction.

title: Development of regiodivergent asymmetric reductive coupling reactions of allenamides to access heteroatom-rich organic compounds
rationale: The article describes regiodivergent asymmetric reductive coupling reactions of allenamides, which are catalytic coupling reactions forming C-heteroatom bonds (C-N, C-O). The abstract and title indicate this is a homogeneous catalytic process using metal catalysts (typically Ni with phosphine ligands) for reductive coupling chemistry.

title: Weakly coordinating tert-amide assisted Rh(III)-catalyzed C4-cyanation of indoles: application in photophysical studies
rationale: Rh(III)-catalyzed C-H cyanation of indoles using NCTS as coupling partner forms C-C bonds. The catalyst [Cp*Rh(MeCN)3][SbF6]2 is a soluble molecular complex with Cp* ligand, operating homogeneously in solution.

title: Construction of unsymmetrical heterobiaryls via the Cp*Rh(III)-catalysed C-H/C-H coupling of heteroarenes
rationale: Cp*Rh(III)-catalyzed C-H/C-H cross-coupling of heteroarenes to form unsymmetrical heterobiaryls (C-C bonds). The catalyst [Cp*RhCl2]2 is a soluble molecular complex with Cp* (pentamethylcyclopentadienyl) ligand, operating homogeneously in solution.

title: Enhancing reductive C-N coupling of nitrocompounds through interfacial engineering of MoO2 in thin carbon layers
rationale: The article describes 'reductive C-N coupling of nitrocompounds' using interfacial engineered MoO2 in thin carbon layers. The catalyst is a solid material (MoO2 embedded in carbon layers) prepared through coating and carbonization, operating in a different phase from reactants, making it heterogeneous. The metal is molybdenum (Mo), supported on carbon material. The bond formed is C-N.

title: Promoting nonsymmetric C-C coupling to valuable oxygenates without metal catalysts in alkali aqueous medium
rationale: The article describes alkali-catalyzed nonsymmetric C-C coupling of formate to form C2-C4 alkanoic acids/alcohols without any metal catalyst participation. The catalysis occurs via alkali (OH⁻) in aqueous medium, which is homogeneous catalysis.

title: Ruthenium-catalysed cross-coupling reaction of ketones with transformable directing groups as alkenyl electrophiles
rationale: The article describes a ruthenium-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between β-ketoamides (as alkenyl electrophiles) and organoboronates to form C(sp2)-C(sp2) bonds. The catalyst is Ru3(CO)12 and other soluble Ru complexes, operating in solution (xylene solvent) as homogeneous catalysts. No solid support is involved, and the ligand is not explicitly specified beyond carbonyl/phosphine in some complexes, so ligand_name is null.

title: Engineering surface lattice hydroxyl groups toward highly efficient photocatalytic methane coupling
rationale: The article describes photocatalytic methane coupling to ethane (C2H6) using Au nanoparticles loaded on Nb3O7(OH) support. This is a heterogeneous catalyst system forming C-C bonds via methane coupling.

title: Halogen-, oxidant- and directing group-free synthesis of donor-acceptor type conjugated polymers
rationale: The article describes a Ru-catalyzed alternating addition polymerization between dialkynylthiophene and dibutadienylpyridine to form conjugated polymers via C-C bond formation. The catalyst [Ru(η6-naphthalene)(η4-oxa-bnd)] is a soluble molecular complex, making it homogeneous catalysis. The oxa-bnd ligand is explicitly mentioned.

title: NHC-catalyzed radical acylation of cycloalkyl silyl peroxides to access 1,6-,1,7-, and 1,8-diketones
rationale: NHC-catalyzed radical acylation forms C-C bonds between aldehydes and cycloalkyl silyl peroxides to produce diketones. The catalyst is a soluble N-heterocyclic carbene (organocatalyst), no metal is involved, and it operates homogeneously in solution.

title: Synthesis of unsymmetrical ketones via dual catalysed cross-coupling of α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acids with aryldiazonium salts
rationale: The article describes a visible-light-enabled cross-coupling reaction between α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acids and aryldiazonium salts to form unsymmetrical ketones, involving decarboxylative aerobic C-C bond cleavage and the creation of new C-C and C-O bonds. The catalysis is dual, with Co(OAc)2·4H2O as a homogeneous metal salt catalyst and Eosin Y as a photoredox catalyst, both operating in solution.

title: Iridium-catalyzed selective arylation of B(6)-H of 3-aryl-o-carboranes with arylboronic acid via direct B-H activation
rationale: Iridium-catalyzed arylation of B-H bonds with arylboronic acids forms C-B bonds, which is a coupling reaction but not C-C, C-O, or C-N. Since C-B coupling is not in the specified list, it should be considered not relevant according to the strict criteria.

title: 9,9′-Bis-o-carboranes: synthesis and exploration of properties
rationale: Pd(OAc)2 is used as a soluble catalyst for oxidative dehydrogenation coupling of carboranes to form 9,9′-bis-o-carboranes, which involves B(9)-H/B(9)-H coupling to form a B-B bond. This is a C-C bond-forming coupling reaction (carborane clusters contain carbon atoms, and the product is a bis-carborane linked through boron vertices, but the overall transformation is a coupling reaction forming new bonds between carbon-containing clusters). The catalyst is homogeneous (soluble Pd salt), no ligand is specified, and no solid support is involved.

title: The low loading of metal in metal-organic framework-derived NiNx@NC promotes amide formation through C-N coupling
rationale: The article describes NiNx@NC (Ni nanoparticles on N-doped carbon) as a heterogeneous catalyst for amide formation via oxidative coupling of aldehydes and amines, which is a C-N bond-forming coupling reaction.

title: Implementation of micelle-enabled C(sp2)-C(sp3) cross-electrophile coupling in pharmaceutical synthesis
rationale: The article describes a micelle-enabled cross-electrophile coupling between aryl and alkyl halides to form C(sp2)-C(sp3) bonds. The catalytic system uses Ni(OAc)2·4H2O with a phenanthroline ligand (L1) and copper as a co-catalyst, all operating in solution under micellar conditions, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Asymmetric 1,2-diaxial synthesis of bi-(hetero)aryl benzofulvene atropisomers via transient directing group-assisted dehydrogenative coupling
rationale: Palladium-catalyzed cross-dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) forming C-C bonds between benzofulvene and bi-(hetero)aryl moieties. The catalyst is Pd(OAc)2 with ligand L1 (chiral ligand) in solution, making it homogeneous. The reaction is explicitly described as converting C-H bonds to C-C bonds via dehydrogenative coupling.

title: Catalysis of surface dispersed Cu2+ species on t-ZrO2: square-planar Cu catalyzed cross-coupling of arylboronic acid and imidazole
rationale: The article describes a heterogeneous Chan-Lam cross-coupling reaction between arylboronic acids and imidazole using CuO/t-ZrO2 catalyst, forming C-N bonds. The catalyst is a solid metal oxide-supported copper material.

title: Silver(I)-catalyzed highly para-selective phosphonation of 2-aryloxazolines
rationale: The article describes a silver-catalyzed cross-dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) reaction forming C-P bonds via para-phosphonation of 2-aryloxazolines. title: Enantioconvergent Reductive C(sp)−C(sp3) Cross-Coupling to Access Chiral α-Alkynyl Phosphonates Under Dual Nickel/Photoredox Catalysis
rationale: The article describes a dual nickel/photoredox-catalyzed enantioconvergent reductive cross-coupling between alkynyl bromides and α-bromo phosphonates to form C(sp)-C(sp3) bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (NiBr2(DME) with ligand L1) operating in solution, making it homogeneous. The reaction forms C-C bonds to create chiral α-alkynyl phosphonates.

title: Visible-Light-Induced N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Catalyzed Single Electron Reduction of Mono-Fluoroarenes
rationale: The article describes an N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-catalyzed, visible-light-induced single electron reduction of mono-fluoroarenes for biaryl cross-couplings. The catalyst is a soluble organic molecule (NHC) operating in solution, making it homogeneous. No metal catalyst is used; the catalysis is purely organocatalytic. The key bond formed is C-C (biaryl coupling).

title: Directed Asymmetric Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive 1,2-Diarylation of Electronically Unactivated Alkenes
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed reductive 1,2-diarylation of alkenes, which is a C-C bond-forming coupling reaction. The catalyst is a soluble nickel salt (Ni(OTf)2, Ni(dme)Cl2, Ni(ClO4)2·6H2O, Ni(BF4)2·6H2O) used with chiral phosphine-oxazoline (PHOX) ligands in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Electroreduction Enables Regioselective 1,2-Diarylation of Alkenes with Two Electrophiles
rationale: The article describes an electrochemical alkene 1,2-diarylation forming C-C bonds. The method explicitly avoids transition-metal catalysts ('avoiding the involvement of transition-metal catalysts'), using aryl nitriles as both radical precursors and redox mediators in an electrolysis setup. This is a homogeneous electrocatalytic system where the redox mediator operates in solution.

title: Nickel-Catalyzed Chemoselective Arylation of Amino Alcohols
rationale: The article describes nickel-catalyzed chemoselective cross-coupling of amino alcohols with aryl chlorides, forming either C-O or C-N bonds depending on conditions. The catalyst is a soluble Ni complex with bisphosphine ligands (specifically CyPAd-DalPhos), making it homogeneous.

title: Enantioselective Radical-Type 1,2-Alkoxy-Phosphinoylation to Styrenes Catalyzed by Chiral Vanadyl Complexes
rationale: The article describes a vanadyl-catalyzed enantioselective 1,2-alkoxy-phosphinoylation of styrenes, forming a C-O bond between the styrene and an alcohol. The catalyst is a soluble chiral vanadyl complex with N-salicylidene-tert-leucinate ligands, operating homogeneously in methanol.

title: Synthesis of P-Stereogenic Phosphine Oxides via Nickel-Catalyzed Asymmetric Cross-Coupling of Secondary Phosphine Oxides with Alkenyl and Aryl Bromides
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed asymmetric cross-coupling forming C-P bonds between secondary phosphine oxides and alkenyl/aryl bromides. This is a coupling reaction, but the bond formed is C-P, which is not among the specified C-C, C-O, or C-N types. The catalyst is a soluble molecular Ni complex (Ni(cod)2) with chiral ligands (e.g., Ph-Phosferrox), indicating homogeneous catalysis.

title: Stereoselective C-Aryl Glycosylation by Catalytic Cross-Coupling of Heteroaryl Glycosyl Sulfones
rationale: The article describes catalytic cross-coupling reactions (Fe- and Ni-catalyzed desulfonylative arylation) between heteroaryl glycosyl sulfones and aromatic nucleophiles/electrophiles to form C-aryl glycosides (C-C bonds). The catalysts are described as 'nonprecious metal catalytic systems' and the reactions involve soluble metal complexes (Fe or Ni with unspecified ligands), indicating homogeneous catalysis.

title: The Sonogashira Coupling on Palladium Milling Balls-A new Reaction Pathway in Mechanochemistry
rationale: The article describes a Sonogashira coupling reaction forming C-C bonds using palladium milling balls or Pd-coated steel balls as the catalyst. The catalyst is solid metal balls operating in a different phase from reactants (mechanochemical conditions), making it heterogeneous. Copper is used as a co-catalyst forming reactive complexes. No soluble molecular catalyst or ligand is used - the active sites are on the metal ball surfaces.

title: Copper-Catalyzed Dynamic Kinetic Asymmetric P−C Coupling of Secondary Phosphine Oxides and Aryl Iodides
rationale: The article describes a copper-catalyzed enantioselective P-C cross-coupling reaction between secondary phosphine oxides and aryl iodides. This is a coupling reaction forming a P-C bond, which is not one of the specified C-C, C-O, or C-N bond types. The catalyst is a copper complex with a chiral 1,2-diamine ligand in solution, indicating homogeneous catalysis.

title: A General and Practical Route to Functionalized Bicyclo[1.1.1]Pentane-Heteroaryls Enabled by Photocatalytic Multicomponent Heteroarylation of [1.1.1]Propellane
rationale: The article describes a photocatalytic multicomponent heteroarylation of [1.1.1]propellane to form C-C bonds, specifically creating bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane-heteroaryls. The method is transition metal-free, using an organic photocatalyst (4CzIPN) in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis without a metal catalyst.

title: Copper-Catalyzed Enantioconvergent Radical C(sp3)−N Cross-Coupling: Access to α,α-Disubstituted Amino Acids
rationale: The article describes a copper-catalyzed enantioconvergent radical C(sp3)-N cross-coupling reaction between alkyl halides and sulfoximines to form C-N bonds. The catalyst is a soluble copper complex with a chiral anionic N,N,N-ligand, operating under homogeneous conditions.

title: Organocatalytic Atroposelective Cross-Coupling of 1-Azonaphthalenes and 2-Naphthols
rationale: The article describes an organocatalytic (chiral Brønsted acid) cross-coupling reaction between 1-azonaphthalenes and 2-naphthols to form axially chiral binaphthyl compounds, which involves C-C bond formation. No transition metal catalyst is used; the catalyst is a soluble chiral Brønsted acid organocatalyst.

title: Csp3−PIII Bond Formation via Cross-Coupling of Umpolung Carbonyls with Phosphine Halides Catalyzed by Nickel
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between hydrazones (Umpolung carbonyls) and phosphine chlorides to form C(sp3)-P bonds. This is a catalytic coupling reaction forming a carbon-heteroatom bond. The catalyst is a soluble nickel complex with NHC ligands (IMes, IPr, IXy, ICy, SIMes, SIPr), making it homogeneous. The bond formed is C-P, which is not among the specified C-C, C-O, or C-N types, so coupling_type is 'unknown'.

The catalysis involves soluble organic catalysts (NHC and photoredox catalysts) in solution, making it homogeneous. No metal catalyst is used; the key catalysts are N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) and organic/organometallic photoredox catalysts (e.g., 3CzClIPN, Ir complexes).

title: Divergent Synthesis of Alcohols and Ketones via Cross-Coupling of Secondary Alcohols under Manganese Catalysis
rationale: The article describes a homogeneous manganese-catalyzed cross-coupling of two secondary alcohols to form γ-disubstituted alcohols and β-disubstituted ketones. This is a dehydrogenative coupling reaction that forms C-C bonds. The catalyst is a well-defined Mn-MACHO complex (a pincer ligand), which operates in solution, making it homogeneous.

title: Atomically Precise Defective Copper Nanocluster Catalysts for Highly Selective C−C Cross-Coupling Reactions

The catalyst is a solid nanocluster material with a defined defect structure, operating in a different phase from the reactants, making it heterogeneous. rationale: The article describes a palladium-catalyzed reductive Heck-type hydroalkenylation and hydroalkynylation of alkenylaldehydes using alkenyl/alkynyl bromides, forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is Pd₂(dba)₃, a soluble molecular complex, indicating homogeneous catalysis. title: Nickel-Catalyzed C−I-Selective C(sp2)−C(sp3) Cross-Electrophile Coupling of Bromo(iodo)arenes with Alkyl Bromides
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile coupling (XEC) reaction forming C(sp2)-C(sp3) bonds between bromo(iodo)arenes and alkyl bromides. The catalyst is a soluble Ni/terpyridine complex operating in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Selective Functionalisation of 5-Methylcytosine by Organic Photoredox Catalysis

The support category is 'Others' as quantum dots are not covered by the other specific categories.

The catalyst system uses NiBr₂·glyme (soluble nickel salt) with a chiral ligand 'L' and an Ir photocatalyst, all operating in solution (MeOAc solvent), making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Photoinduced Electron Transfer from Xanthates to Acyl Azoliums: Divergent Ketone Synthesis via N-Heterocyclic Carbene Catalysis

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Arylation of Endocyclic 1-Azaallyl Anions: Concise Synthesis of Unprotected Enantioenriched cis-2,3-Diarylpiperidines

The catalyst is a soluble Pd complex with phosphine ligands (XPhos, (2R,3R)-iPr-BI-DIME), operating in solution, which defines homogeneous catalysis. The bond formed is C-C (aryl-aryl coupling).

The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (PPh3AuNTf2, IPrAuNTf2) operating in solution, making it homogeneous. The metal is gold (Au), and the key ligand used is triphenylphosphine (PPh3).

title: Visible Light Induced Copper-Catalyzed Enantioselective Deaminative Arylation of Amino Acid Derivatives Assisted by Phenol

title: Dual Catalysis of Gold Nanoclusters: Photocatalytic Cross-Dehydrogenative Coupling by Cooperation of Superatomic Core and Molecularly Modified Staples**

The catalytic metal is gold (Au), and the support is classified as 'Metals' since it consists of unsupported gold nanoclusters. title: Neutral and Anionic Square Planar Palladium(0) Complexes Stabilized by a Silicon Z-Type Ligand

title: Light-Driven Enantioselective Carbene-Catalyzed Radical-Radical Coupling

title: Reductive Cross-Coupling of a Vinyl Thianthrenium Salt and Secondary Alkyl Iodides

rationale: The article describes a cobalt-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction forming C(sp2)-C(sp3) bonds. The catalyst is a molecular cobalt(II) complex with phenoxythiazoline (FTz) ligands, operating in solution as a homogeneous catalyst.

title: Photoexcitation of Distinct Divalent Palladium Complexes in Cross-Coupling Amination Under Air

The optimization table shows ligand screening (bipyridine derivatives), confirming homogeneous catalysis. The reaction forms C-N bonds via excited-state Pd(II) catalysis.
