The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (cationic [Ru(II)(η6-p-cymene)(NHC-SO)Cl]+), making it homogeneous.

title: Synthesis of (Hetero)biaryls via Nickel Catalyzed Reductive Cross-Electrophile Coupling Between (Hetero)aryl Iodides and Bromides
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed reductive cross-electrophile coupling between (hetero)aryl iodides and bromides to form C(sp2)-C(sp2) bonds. The catalyst is NiBr2·DME with 2,2'-bipyridine ligand, forming a soluble molecular complex in solution, which is homogeneous catalysis.

title: Expedited Proton Relay in Enzyme-Inspired Cobaloximes Facilitate Organic Transformations
rationale: The article describes a photocatalytic amination reaction (forming C-N bonds) using soluble cobaloxime complexes (Cl-Co-X with axial imidazole or L-histidine coordination) as catalysts. The reaction is a cross-coupling approach for aniline synthesis, and the catalyst operates homogeneously in solution.

title: Direct Access to Benzolactams and Benzolactones via Nickel Catalyzed Carbonylation with CO2
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile carbonylation using CO2 to form isoindolinones (γ-lactams) and isobenzofuranones (γ-lactones). This involves C-C bond formation between an aryl halide and CO2, followed by intramolecular cyclization. The catalyst is a soluble molecular Ni(phen)Cl2 complex, making it homogeneous. The key ligand is phenanthroline (phen).

title: Electrochemical Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling with Nucleophiles
rationale: Electrochemical decarboxylative cross-coupling of carboxylic acids with various nucleophiles (fluorine, alcohol, H2O, acid, amine) forms C-C, C-O, and C-N bonds. The reaction is electrocatalyzed without transition metal catalysts (metal-free), using electrodes (carbon cloth anode, Pt cathode) in a homogeneous electrochemical system.

title: Multicomponent Synthesis of 3(2H)-Furanones Initiated by Copper(II)-Catalyzed Alkyne-Carbonyl Cross Metathesis
rationale: The article describes a copper(II)-catalyzed alkyne-carbonyl cross metathesis as the initial step in a multicomponent synthesis of 3(2H)-furanones, forming two C-O bonds in the final heterocycle. The catalyst is a soluble metal salt (Cu(OTf)2) used in solution, making it homogeneous. No solid support or specific ligand is mentioned for the key catalytic step.

title: Copper-Mediated Synthesis of N-Aryl-Oxamic Acids
rationale: The article describes a Cu-catalyzed Ullmann-Goldberg cross-coupling between aryl iodides and oxamates to form N-aryloxamates (C-N bond formation). The catalyst is a soluble Cu(I) salt (CuI) with a diamine ligand (L1), operating in a homogeneous phase.

title: Mapping Electrophile Chemoselectivity in DalPhos/Nickel N-Arylation Catalysis: The Unusual Influence of Remote Sterics
rationale: The article describes nickel-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (N-arylation) using soluble bisphosphine ligands (DalPhos and DPPF) in a homogeneous catalytic system.

title: Introduction of Molecular Complexity via the Cross-Coupling of Lithium 1,4-Dioxene with Aryl Bromides
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between lithium 1,4-dioxene and aryl bromides to form 2-aryl-1,4-dioxenes (C-C bond formation). The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (Pd2(dba)3/XPhos), making it homogeneous. The key ligand is XPhos.

title: Photoelectrocatalytic [4+2] Annulation for S-Heterocycle Assembly Enabled by Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer (PCET)
rationale: The article describes a photoelectrocatalytic [4+2] annulation forming isothiochromenes via cross-dehydrogenative coupling (CDC), which is a C-C bond forming reaction. The catalyst is [Mes-Acr⁺]ClO₄⁻, an organic photocatalyst (acridinium salt) used in solution, making it homogeneous. No transition metal catalyst is used (metal: none).

title: Organic Two-Photon-Absorbing Photosensitizers Can Overcome Competing Light Absorption in Organic Photocatalysis
rationale: The article describes organic two-photon-absorbing photosensitizers used for photocatalytic Sonogashira Csp2-Csp cross-coupling and Csp2-N cross-coupling reactions. The catalysts are metal-free organic chromophores operating in solution (homogeneous), forming both C-C and C-N bonds.

title: Syntheses of Diarylmethanes Via an Oxidative Benzylic Functionalization of P-Alkyl Phenol Derivatives Under Quaternary Ammonium Hypoiodite Catalysis
rationale: The article describes a quaternary ammonium hypoiodite (Bu4NI)-catalyzed oxidative benzylic functionalization of p-alkyl phenols to form diarylmethane derivatives via coupling with electron-rich aromatics. This is a C-C bond-forming coupling reaction. The catalyst is tetrabutylammonium iodide, a soluble organic salt, making it homogeneous. No transition metal is used.

title: Copper(II)-Catalyzed Amination of Aryl Chlorides in Aqueous Ammonia
rationale: The article describes a Cu(II)-catalyzed amination of aryl chlorides with aqueous ammonia, forming C-N bonds. The catalyst is a soluble copper salt (CuSO4) with an organic ligand (4,7-dimethoxy-1,10-phenanthroline) operating in aqueous solution, making it homogeneous. This is a copper-catalyzed Ullmann-type coupling reaction.

title: Formate Salt as a Bifunctional Reagent for Hydroxylation and Carbonylation Reactions Under Photochemically Driven Nickel Catalysis
rationale: The article describes a photochemically driven nickel-catalyzed hydroxylation reaction using formate salt to synthesize phenol derivatives (forming C-O bonds). The catalyst system uses NiBr2.diglyme as a precatalyst with 4,4'-dtbbpy ligand and 5CzBN photocatalyst in solution, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Transition-Metal Free Amination and Hydrodefluorination of Aryl Fluorides Promoted by Solvated Electrons
rationale: The article describes a transition-metal-free C-N coupling reaction (amination) of aryl fluorides using solvated electrons generated from lithium and sonication. The method explicitly eliminates the need for transition metal catalysts, operating via a radical-nucleophilic substitution (SRN1) mechanism. Table 1 shows that the reaction proceeds without the nickel catalyst (entry 4 vs. 2), confirming it is metal-free. The catalysis is homogeneous as the active species (solvated electrons) are generated and act in solution.

title: O-p-Methoxyphenyl α-Hydroxycarboxylic Acids as Versatile Hydroxyalkylation Agents for Photocatalysis
rationale: The article describes Pd-catalyzed allylation and Ni-catalyzed arylation/alkenylation reactions using α-hydroxy radicals as coupling partners, forming C-C bonds. The catalysts are soluble transition metal complexes (Pd and Ni) operating in solution, making them homogeneous. No solid support is mentioned, and no specific ligand names are provided in the given text.

title: Electrochemical Enantioselective Nickel-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling of Aldehydes with Aryl Iodides
rationale: The article describes a nickel-catalyzed electrochemical cross-coupling between aldehydes and aryl iodides to form diarylmethanols (C-C bond formation). The catalyst is a soluble molecular Ni complex with a chiral cyano-bis(oxazoline) ligand (L2), operating in solution, making it homogeneous.

title: Reusable Iron-Copper Catalyzed Cross-Coupling of Primary Amides with Aryl and Alkyl Halides: Access to N-Arylamides as Potential Antibacterial and Anticancer Agents
rationale: The article describes an iron-copper catalyzed cross-coupling of primary amides with aryl/alkyl halides to form N-arylamides (C-N bonds). The catalyst is described as 'reusable' and 'ligand-free,' and characterization techniques (XPS, XRD) suggest a solid, heterogeneous material. The catalyst is not specified as a common support type (metal oxides, carbon, etc.), so it is classified as 'Others'.

title: Easily Accessible and Solution-Stable Ni(0) Precatalysts for High-Throughput Experimentation
rationale: The article describes Ni(0) precatalysts (DAB-Ni-COD complexes) used in Suzuki (C-C) and C-N coupling reactions. The catalysts are soluble molecular complexes in organic solvents, making them homogeneous.

title: Rapid and Sustainable Electrochemical Pd Catalyst Generation from Bulk Metal
rationale: The article describes a Suzuki cross-coupling reaction (C-C bond formation) catalyzed by Pd species generated electrochemically from bulk Pd metal. The catalyst is generated as nanoparticles or soluble complexes in ionic liquid medium, but the active species originate from a solid bulk metal electrode, making it heterogeneous. The support category is 'Metals' since it uses unsupported bulk Pd metal as the source.

title: Nickel/Photoredox Catalyzed Aryl-Alkyl Cross-Coupling with Alkyl Boronic Esters as Radical Precursors
rationale: The article describes a nickel/photoredox dual-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between aryl halides and alkyl boronic esters to form C(sp2)-C(sp3) bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular nickel complex (NiBr2·DME) with a dtbbpy ligand, operating in solution with a photoredox catalyst, making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Nickel-Catalyzed O-Arylation of N-Protected Amino Alcohols with (Hetero)aryl Chlorides
rationale: The article describes Ni-catalyzed C-O cross-coupling (O-arylation) of N-protected amino alcohols with (hetero)aryl chlorides, which is a coupling reaction forming C-O bonds. The catalyst is a soluble Ni complex with ancillary ligands (CyPAd-DalPhos, L1; CgPhen-DalPhos, L2), making it homogeneous catalysis.

title: Modular Synthesis of Arylpyridylmethylamines via Visible-Light-Driven Reductive Coupling of Amines, Aldehydes, and Pyridines
rationale: The article describes a visible-light-driven reductive coupling of amines, aldehydes, and pyridines to form arylpyridylmethylamines, which involves C-N bond formation. The abstract explicitly states the reaction proceeds 'without the need for any transition-metal catalysts, photocatalysts, and acid additives,' indicating a metal-free, homogeneous process. The coupling is a multicomponent reaction forming a C-N bond between an amine and a pyridylmethyl group.

title: Ar-X Coupling Reactions of Cationic Aryl Copper(II) Complexes with Organic Substrates: What Role Do Radicals Play?
rationale: The article studies cationic copper(II) aryl complexes [(phen)Cu(Ar)]+ as intermediates in copper-catalyzed C-X cross-coupling reactions (Ullmann-type reactions). The research explicitly examines C-C, C-S, and Ar-I bond-forming reactions via gas-phase experiments and DFT calculations, focusing on fundamental mechanistic aspects of coupling transformations. The catalyst is a soluble molecular copper complex with phenanthroline ligand, making it homogeneous.

title: Choline Chloride/Urea - Promoted Iodocyclization of 3-Alkynylthiophene-2-carboxamides: A Green Synthesis of 4-Iodo-7H-thieno[2,3-c]pyran-7-imines and Their Coupling Reactions in Deep Eutectic Solvents
rationale: The article describes Pd-catalyzed Sonogashira and Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions (C-C bond formation) performed in deep eutectic solvents. The catalyst is a soluble Pd complex (PdCl2(PPh3)2 and Pd(OAc)2 with PPh3 are mentioned in the full text), which is homogeneous. The main focus is on the iodocyclization, but the subsequent coupling reactions are explicitly described and are the subject of catalysis.

title: Ru-Catalyzed Deoxygenative Functionalization of Phenols via π-Coordination Activation: Mechanochemical Access to N-Aryl Amides and α-Aryl Carbonyls
rationale: The article describes a Ru-catalyzed direct amidation of phenols with primary amides to form N-aryl amides (C-N bond formation) via a mechanochemical approach. The catalyst is a ruthenium complex operating in solution/mechanochemical conditions, making it homogeneous. No specific ligand is mentioned in the provided text, and no solid support is involved.

title: Data-Driven Prediction of Reactivity and Additive Selection for C(sp2)-(Hetero)Atom Bond Couplings in an Adaptive Dynamic Homogeneous Catalysis
rationale: The article describes a homogeneous nickel-catalyzed adaptive dynamic homogeneous catalysis (AD-HoC) platform for visible-light-driven C(sp2)-(hetero)atom bond formation, specifically mentioning C(sp2)-N, C(sp2)-S, and C(sp2)-C bond couplings. The catalyst is a soluble nickel complex operating in solution.

title: Modular Synthesis of Unsymmetrical 1,1'-Disubstituted Ferrocenes by Sequential Suzuki-Miyaura Cross-Coupling of 1,1'-Diborylferrocene
rationale: The article describes a Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling (SMCC) reaction, which is a Pd-catalyzed C-C bond-forming coupling. The catalyst used is Pd(dppf)Cl2, a soluble molecular complex in solution, making it homogeneous. The ligand is dppf. No solid support is involved.

title: Engineering of the Thiamine Diphosphate-Dependent JanthE for the Synthesis of Tertiary Alcohols
rationale: The article describes JanthE, a thiamine diphosphate-dependent enzyme that catalyzes aldehyde-ketone cross-coupling reactions to form C-C bonds, producing tertiary alcohols. This is a biocatalytic coupling reaction. The catalyst is an enzyme (soluble protein), so catalysis_type is homogeneous. No metal catalyst is used, so metal is 'none'. Since it's homogeneous, support is null. The cofactor is thiamine diphosphate, but it's not a ligand in the organometallic sense, so ligand_name is null. The bond formed is C-C.

title: Ir/Ni Metallaphotoredox Catalysis for the C(sp3)─H Bond α-Arylation and Alkylation of N-Alkyl N-Heterocycles
rationale: The article describes a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed C(sp3)-H α-arylation and alkylation of N-alkyl heterocycles using soluble Ir photocatalyst [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbbpy)][PF6] and NiCl2(dtbbpy) complex. This is a homogeneous dual catalytic system for C-C bond formation via cross-coupling.

title: Well-Defined [Pd(NHC)(η3-methylnaphthyl)Br] Complexes in Cross-Coupling Reactions
rationale: Article describes well-defined Pd(II)-NHC complexes as pre-catalysts for Suzuki-Miyaura (C-C) and Buchwald-Hartwig (C-N) coupling reactions. The catalysts are molecular complexes operating in solution, making them homogeneous.

title: Photoredox-Catalyzed Hydroalkylation of C(sp3)-H Acids
rationale: The article describes a photoredox-catalyzed hydroalkylation (C-C bond formation) using CeCl3 or Ce(OTf)3 as a homogeneous metal catalyst in solution. The catalyst is a soluble cerium salt, operating in a photoredox cycle to enable radical coupling reactions.

title: Copper Single Atoms Chelated on Ligand-Modified Carbon for Ullmann-Type C−O Coupling
rationale: The article describes a heterogeneous single-atom catalyst (copper on ligand-modified carbon) designed specifically for Ullmann-type C-O coupling, which is a bond-forming coupling reaction.

title: Nickel-Catalyzed P-Arylation of HP(= O)(R/OR)2 Nucleophiles with (Hetero)Aryl Chlorides Enabled by DalPhos Ligation
rationale: The article describes nickel-catalyzed C-P cross-coupling (P-arylation) using soluble nickel/DalPhos complexes, forming C-P bonds between (hetero)aryl chlorides and HP(O)(R)2/HP(O)(OR)2 nucleophiles. This is a homogeneous coupling reaction.

title: Copper Single Atoms Chelated on Ligand-Modified Carbon for Ullmann-type C−O Coupling
rationale: The article describes a heterogeneous catalyst (Cu single atoms on functionalized graphite nanoplatelets) for Ullmann-type C-O coupling between phenols and aryl halides. The catalyst is a solid material (Cu@f-GNPs) with copper atoms chelated to a tetraethylenepentamine-pyrrole ligand immobilized on a carbon support.

title: Chloromethylation of Lignin as a Route to Functional Material with Catalytic Properties in Cross-Coupling and Click Reactions
rationale: The article describes a lignin-supported Pd/CuO nanoparticle catalyst (Lignin@Pd/CuO-NPs) used for Suzuki-Miyaura, Heck, and Sonogashira cross-coupling reactions, all of which form C-C bonds. The catalyst is solid and operates in a different phase from reactants, making it heterogeneous. The support is modified lignin, which falls under 'Others' as it is a biopolymer-based material not covered by other categories.

title: Photocatalyzed Oxidative Tandem Reaction Mediated by Bipyridinium for Multifunctional Derivatization of Alcohols
rationale: The article describes a photocatalytic esterification reaction (forming C-O bonds) from alcohols using bipyridinium-based small molecule photocatalysts. The catalyst is a soluble organic molecule (bipyridinium derivatives) operating in solution, making it homogeneous. The process is explicitly described as metal- and additive-free, so metal is 'none'. The coupling type is ester formation (C-O bond formation).

title: Ambient Electroreductive Carboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Chlorides and Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) Upgrading
rationale: The article describes a nickel-pincer complex catalyzing the electrochemical carboxylation of alkyl chlorides and PVC with CO2, forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is a soluble molecular complex (Ni-pincer), making it homogeneous. The transformation is a reductive cross-coupling where a C-Cl bond is activated and coupled with CO2 to form a carboxylic acid (new C-C bond).

title: Upcycling of Chitin to Cross-Coupling Catalysts: Tailored Supports and Opportunities in Mechanochemistry
rationale: Article describes Pd nanoparticles supported on N-doped carbons derived from chitin for Heck and Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions, forming C-C bonds. The catalyst is solid and operates in a different phase from reactants, making it heterogeneous with carbon support.

title: Chloromethylation of Lignin as a Route to Functional Material with Catalytic Properties in Cross-Coupling and Click Reactions
rationale: The article describes a lignin-supported Pd/Cu nanoparticle catalyst used for multiple C-C bond formation reactions (cross-coupling) and click reactions. The catalyst is a solid material (lignin-based support with metal nanoparticles), making it heterogeneous. The metals are Pd and Cu, the support is derived from lignin (classified as Carbon), and the primary bond formed is C-C.

title: Access to Substituted 1,1-Diarylalkanes by Friedel-Crafts Benzylations Mediated by FeCl3-based Deep Eutectic Solvents
rationale: The article describes a Friedel-Crafts benzylation reaction forming C-C bonds between arenes and benzylating reagents. The catalyst is FeCl3-based Deep Eutectic Solvent (DES), which is a homogeneous liquid system where FeCl3 acts as a Lewis acid catalyst dissolved in the DES medium. No solid support is involved, and no specific ligand is mentioned for the iron catalyst.

title: Remote Migratory Reductive Arylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by Electrochemical Nickel Catalysis
rationale: The article describes an electrochemical nickel-catalyzed reductive cross-coupling between aryl halides and unactivated alkenes to form C(sp2)-C(sp3) bonds (C-C coupling). The catalyst is a soluble Ni salt (NiI2) with a ligand (L1) in solution, making it homogeneous. The reaction is a migratory reductive arylation, a type of C-C bond-forming coupling.

title: Ni/PiNe Heterogeneous Catalyst from Biomass Waste: Low-Loading, Ligand-Free Suzuki-Miyaura Cross-Coupling
rationale: The article describes a Ni-based heterogeneous catalyst (Ni/PiNe) derived from pine needles (biomass waste) for Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling, which forms C-C bonds. The catalyst is solid and operates in a different phase from reactants, and the support is carbonaceous (from biomass).

title: Mechanochemical Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling of Thianthrenium Salts and Arylboronic Acids
rationale: The article describes a Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-type cross-coupling between thianthrenium salts and arylboronic acids to form biaryls (C-C bonds). The catalyst system uses Pd(OAc)2 with RuPhos ligand under mechanochemical conditions, indicating a homogeneous molecular catalyst in solution (liquid-assisted grinding with Me-THF).

title: Liquid Humins: A Sustainable Carbonaceous Feedstock for Pd/C Catalysts Design with a Reduced
rationale: The article describes Pd/C catalysts (palladium on carbon supports) used for Suzuki-Miyaura and Mizoroki-Heck coupling reactions, which are classic C-C bond-forming transformations. The catalyst is a solid material (Pd on carbon support) operating in a different phase from reactants, making it heterogeneous.

title: Modulating Catalytic Selectivity via NiZn-CdS Interface for Visible-Light Mediated Suzuki Cross-Coupling and Standalone NiZn Alloy for Ambient Synthesis of 1,2,3-Triazoles
rationale: The article describes a NiZn alloy and NiZn-CdS nanocomposite as heterogeneous catalysts for Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling (SMCC), which is a C-C bond-forming reaction. The catalyst is a solid bimetallic alloy and composite material, operating in a different phase from the reactants.

title: Mechanochemical Generation of Active Pd/BippyPhos Catalyst for Efficient C?N Cross-Coupling in Air
rationale: The article describes a Buchwald-Hartwig amination (C-N bond-forming cross-coupling) catalyzed by a palladium complex generated from [Pd(π-cinnamyl)Cl]2 and bulky phosphine ligands (BippyPhos/t-BuXPhos). The catalyst is formed in situ via mechanochemical activation in the solid state, but the active species is a soluble molecular Pd-phosphine complex, as confirmed by solid-state NMR, operating in a homogeneous manner during the coupling reaction.

title: Atomically Dispersed Palladium Promoted Suzuki-Miyaura Cross Coupling
rationale: The article describes a Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction (C-C bond formation) catalyzed by atomically dispersed palladium supported on polymeric carbon nitride (Pd/PCN). The catalyst is a solid material (Pd atoms stabilized on PCN support) operating in a different phase from reactants, making it heterogeneous. The support is classified as 'Nitride' since polymeric carbon nitride (PCN) is a carbon nitride material. No ligand is mentioned for the main catalytic system.

title: Pd
rationale: The article describes a Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling (SMCC) reaction forming C─C bonds to create a porous organic polymer. The catalyst used is Pd-based, and after pyrolysis, it becomes a heterogeneous catalyst with Pd nanoclusters and single atoms doped into a nanocarbon matrix (PdNC/Pd-NC800).

title: Porous Supramolecular Assemblies for Efficient Suzuki Coupling of Aryl Chlorides
rationale: The article describes a Suzuki coupling reaction (C-C bond formation) catalyzed by palladium. The catalyst is a porous supramolecular assembly/polymer (porous organic polymer) formed via a ligand-template approach, which is a solid material that operates in a different phase from the reactants, making it heterogeneous. The support is a porous organic polymer, which falls under 'Others'. The ligand (tris-3-pyridylphosphine) is encapsulated within the assembly but is part of the solid framework, not a soluble molecular complex.

title: Lead-Free Cs3Bi2Br9 Perovskite as Heterogeneous Photocatalyst for Oxidative Dehydrogenative Coupling of Thiols and P(O)H Compounds
rationale: The article describes a cross-dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) reaction between thiols and P(O)H compounds to form S-P(O) bonds, which is a coupling reaction. The catalyst is lead-free Cs3Bi2Br9 perovskite, a solid material used as a heterogeneous photocatalyst. The catalytic metal is not a transition metal; the perovskite contains Bi, which is a main group element, so 'metal' is set to 'none'. The support category is 'Others' as perovskite materials are not covered by the other categories. The bond formed is S-P(O), which is not C-C, C-O, or C-N, so coupling_type is 'unknown'.

title: Rational Design of Highly Porous Donor-Acceptor Based Conjugated Microporous Polymer for Photocatalytic Benzylamine Coupling Reaction
rationale: The article describes a photocatalytic benzylamine coupling reaction (C═N bond formation) using a conjugated microporous polymer (CBZ-CMP) as a heterogeneous, metal-free catalyst. The catalyst is a solid organic polymer material, classified as 'Others' for support.

title: Functionalized Bottlebrush Polymers as Bioinspired Photocatalysts for Highly Efficient Organic Transformations
rationale: The article describes photocatalytic organic transformations using bottlebrush polymers incorporating bipyridine-nickel complexes. The catalysts are soluble in aqueous media (water-soluble polymers), making them homogeneous. The transformations include Csp2-Csp3 cross-couplings, which are C-C bond forming reactions.
